method.interpretation: lower value = closer to decision boundary
method.comparison: helped (pure wrong, hybrid right) vs hurt (pure right, hybrid wrong)
method.note: GDN uses h12-1 (h3-1 unavailable at 1.3B); RetNet/HGRN2 use h3-1

narrative_text: All 3 architectures show hurt samples have significantly lower pure-model confidence margins than helped samples (all p < 1e-60, Cohen d > 1.2). This is the OPPOSITE of the borderline hypothesis: attention does NOT primarily help borderline cases. Instead, attention corrects high-confidence errors (helped: mean margin ~2.5) while disrupting low-confidence correct predictions (hurt: mean margin ~1.0-1.5). The pure model confidence is a strong predictor of whether attention will help or hurt on a given example.

rebuttal_implications.finding: Attention effect is NOT opaque w.r.t. confidence margin. Hurt samples cluster near the decision boundary; helped samples are confidently wrong under pure model.
rebuttal_implications.rebuttal_use: If reviewer asks why attention helps/hurts unpredictably: confidence margin analysis shows attention systematically rescues high-confidence errors and destabilizes borderline-correct predictions. The effect is predictable from pure-model confidence, even though surface/perplexity features show no signal.
